program: Violence intervention, trauma support, education and employment

what: Chicago CRED combines outreach, trauma therapy and life coaching for people at high risk of gun violence.
It helps participants pursue education, paid work experience and employment.
CRED also funds community partners and supports Chicago’s violence-intervention network.
strengths: A sustained local service model reaches people facing severe violence and employment barriers.
Original evaluations examine participants, service dosage and neighborhood outcomes.
Therapy and supported employment offer plausible complementary health and resource mechanisms.
reservations: Participant victimization was null in the original evaluation, and completers are selected.
Current causal net earnings, trauma utility and additional annual cohorts remain unverified.
Whole-recipient grant costs, overlapping public CVI and marginal donor replacement complicate attribution.

sections.what: Chicago CRED Inc, EIN 81-3130448, is the legal recipient. Its official site now links a current Give Lively donation page, replacing the closed historical Network for Good campaign. The linked page was accessible, but no transaction or fulfillment was verified. South and West Side service delivery establishes Chicago beneficiaries despite the tax filing's California address. [Current services](https://www.chicagocred.org/)
sections.monitoring: The 2025 impact report separates direct services from grants and ecosystem work but does not establish causal avoided injury or net household resources. Its cumulative grants and multi-organization historical shooting estimates are not current annual CRED-only outcomes. Current employment services include paid internships and a year of coaching after placement. The official donation link reaches Give Lively; no transaction was performed. Follow-up needs current unique entrants, phase completion, clinical dose, validated trauma scores, victimization and net earnings, not only placements or gross pay.
sections.qualitative: The original 2023 PNAS paper is a quasi-experimental comparison of 324 recruited men and 2,500 matched peers, including 111 alumni. It cannot identify randomized intent-to-treat effects. No phase showed a discernible victimization improvement. The alumni arrest association is not an injury coefficient: remaining long enough to graduate excludes fatalities and some high-risk departures, while police records introduce measurement bias. The May 2026 CORNERS summary adds updated comparisons and neighborhood findings, but acknowledges overlapping CVI coverage; survey changes do not supply a causal dollar or utility effect. These sources strengthen mechanism and counterfactual assessment, not the numerical injury, trauma or earnings priors. Completion, injury-null and unknown cases retain this uncertainty.
sections.cost:
Calendar 2024 original Form 990-PF reports $36,314,414 total book expenses. Its $37,047,914 charitable cash disbursements are a different accounting measure, not an addback. The whole recognized annual recipient cost includes direct work, grants, administration and other activities; it is not a restricted participant-program denominator. No equivalent Form 990 netted event/rental addback was identified. Outside implementation and social costs remain separate.

A judged 400 local household opportunities and .5 annual-package response imply 200 exposed households, with 100 clinical participants. A .05 annual victimization risk and .05 causal reduction imply .25 avoided physical victimizations. One integrated injury QALY per event is truncated within three years and excludes trauma. The remaining 99.75 people receive .03 trauma utility for half a year. Positive clinical components retain .8 for overlap; harms remain full. A one-year delay and 3% discount produce 1.356311 clinical QALYs.

The clinical cohort is a subset of the 200 resource-exposed households; one participant household carries one modeled welfare-equivalent person, with other family welfare unpriced. Resource exposure remains when clinical benefit fails. Fifty households have judged net job resources of $1,500 and net stipends of $300. Positive components each retain .5, then full attendance costs of $300 are subtracted: $600 net. The other 150 households net −$150. Negative components are never attenuated by overlap. A single joint household log gives .5 × [50 log(1.04) + 150 log(.99)] / 1.03 = .220138 equivalent healthy years at a $15,000 household baseline for one finite year. Combined 1.576449 yields $230.355757 million per ten combined equivalents, not ten clinical QALYs.

Job gains are after taxes, benefit withdrawal, replacement earnings and new-job commuting or care costs; stipends are after taxes and benefits. Class attendance, early foregone work and travel are separate full burdens. These amounts are hypotheses, not observed gains. No ordinary survivor wages are added. Central payer and external care incidence is unknown-neutral, not factual zero. Matched stipend-payer losses, external costs, negative resource changes, adverse trauma and mixed-sign cases are explicit. Household gains and losses combine before one log; distinct payer households are modeled separately. Whole portfolio and nonlocal incidence remain unknown.

This deep review retains the initial conditional center unchanged, not an empirically calibrated complete-portfolio estimate. Fiscal 2024 grants of $10,552,266 are already in $36,314,414 book expenses. A direct-service numerator is deliberately incomplete against the whole-recipient denominator; unknown grant and neighborhood benefits and burdens are not asserted zero. The 0.5 funded-work response is a conditional annual counterfactual, not a measured next-gift effect. A 111/324 uptake sensitivity uses historical completer selection only as a throughput hypothesis, not current efficacy.

Finite job-duration cases distinguish one-off stipends and attendance disruption from recurring net job resources. When employment starts in the same year, first-year stipend, net jobs and full process costs enter one joint household log. Later years contain only net job resources, including taxes, benefit withdrawal and new-work commuting or care; no stipend or attendance cost repeats. Delayed employment must start after the first-year window, avoiding overlapping same-household logs. Zero job duration keeps the stipend and full process burden. Added tax/care inputs are incremental stresses beyond the already-net central $1,500, not claims about observed component amounts. Matching payer cases represent distinct displaced beneficiaries or outside providers, not charging the donating household twice for expenditure already in annual cost. Complete world incidence remains unknown.
sections.funding: Comparable calendar 2022, 2023 and 2024 book expenses are $34,196,858, $33,370,210 and $36,314,414, mean $34,627,160.67. Contributions in 2024 are $26,010,890 and net assets $16,146,226. The current impact report describes CRED as privately funded while partners increasingly receive public support. This is not evidence that an additional gift expands services rather than replacing another donor. The .5 response prior judges additional annual funded work against alternatives; b=1 shows full response. No specific marginal expansion cost was verified. Existing coalition appropriations and historical projects are not credited anew. [Original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202522209349101107/IRS990PF)

model.geographicAttribution: Chicago South and West Side household cohort; clinical participants are a subset of resource exposure.
model.formula: Clinical health is discounted integrated injury benefit plus time-sliced finite trauma utility, positive-only clinical overlap, minus full exposed-union harm. For each disjoint household group and nonoverlapping year, net positive-only-overlap job/stipend components minus full negative resources and burdens enter 0.5 × households × discounted years × log(1 + net / annual consumption baseline). Headline counts signed resources once alongside health and full annual book expenses plus separately identified external cost.
model.counterfactual: Existing public CVI, alternative employment, therapy, other donors and partner grants continue. Annual additional funded work is conditional; neither all grant outcomes nor next-gift expansion is identified.
model.attribution: All population, risk, uptake, response, efficacy and resource success coefficients are conditional judgments, not recipient causal observations.
model.uncertainty: Conditional reference retains prior judgments. Original individual victimization null, completer selection and overlapping neighborhood interventions do not calibrate injury/PTSD or employment coefficients. Current unique households, actual dose and net income, outside incidence, portfolio effects and marginal funding remain unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional completed services, prevented gunshot victimization and finite trauma relief, plus actual net household earnings and stipend resources; not arrests, graduation counts, placement salaries, cumulative grants or ecosystem totals converted directly to welfare.
